inputs.original_text: The Punjab and Haryana High Court is right that bail should not be revoked on suspicion alone. But bail is not a clean bill of health, and serious allegations involving stolen property should not be waved away either. The burden is on investigators to build a solid case and show any misuse of liberty; courts must apply that standard consistently. A justice system that protects the accused while taking public safety and victims seriously is essential to public trust.
inputs.modified_text: Bail should never be revoked on suspicion alone, but it is a conditional privilege—not a declaration of innocence. Allegations involving stolen property deserve serious, disciplined investigation, not dismissal or excuses. Investigators must prove their case and demonstrate any misuse of liberty, while courts apply the same standard consistently. When victims and public safety seem secondary, confidence in the justice system erodes. Protecting due process and maintaining order are both essential.
